implemented_requirements.evidence: index.html contains a <section id="grid" class="grid"> element and ui.js declares a renderGrid() method that creates tiles for each word.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Select four words at a time
implemented_requirements.evidence: game.js defines a toggleSelect(word) method and a selected array; ui.js has onTileClick(word) and updateSelection() stubs.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Submit a guess and receive feedback
implemented_requirements.evidence: game.js declares submitGuess() returning a result object with type 'correct'|'one-away'|'wrong'; ui.js has handleGuessResult(result) and toast/animation methods.
game.js lists a shuffleRemaining() method and index.html includes a Shuffle button wired to UI.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Track mistakes with a maximum of four
implemented_requirements.evidence: game.js defines mistakes, maxMistakes = 4, but no code shows decrementing or loss condition enforcement.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Reveal correct groups with category name and difficulty color
implemented_requirements.evidence: ui.js has revealGroup(categoryIndex) and a solved‑groups section, but no implementation details, no color‑coding logic, and no evidence of difficulty mapping (yellow, green, blue, purple).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Ensure only one correct solution exists
implemented_requirements.evidence: No data or validation logic is present to guarantee uniqueness of the solution.
puzzles.js provides getDailyPuzzle() that selects a puzzle from a PUZZLES array based on the current date.
ui.js includes showToast(), animateWrong(), animateOneAway() which are intended to give instant feedback, though implementations are not shown.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Wire up the game (main entry point)
implemented_requirements.evidence: main.js is empty; there is no code that creates a ConnectionsGame instance, connects it to GameUI, or starts the game loop.

critical_issues: game.js contains only method signatures and comments; core game logic (selection handling, guess validation, mistake counting, win/loss detection) is missing.
ui.js class methods are declared but their bodies are omitted (represented by ellipsis), so no UI rendering or interaction occurs.
main.js, the entry point that should instantiate the game and UI, is empty, meaning the application cannot start.
No PUZZLES data is provided; getDailyPuzzle() references a PUZZLES array that does not exist in the repository.
Color‑coded difficulty display and category reveal are not implemented, violating a core visual requirement.
There is no enforcement of the four‑mistake limit or any loss condition handling in the provided code.
judge.summary: The repository contains skeletal files that outline the intended architecture (game logic class, UI class, daily puzzle selector) and UI markup, but the actual implementations are missing. Critical functionality such as game state updates, guess validation, mistake tracking, win/loss handling, color‑coded difficulty display, and the application entry point are absent. Consequently, the solution does not meet the core requirements and is unlikely to run as a functional puzzle game.
